instruction: Guide me through downloading, installing, and applying the Fluent GTK theme from GitHub on my GNOME desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires agent to download and install Fluent GTK theme from GitHub and apply it using GNOME settings. Evaluator checks if gtk-theme setting contains 'Fluent' by executing gsettings command and checking the output. Uses existing framework functions (check_list metric + cache_file getter). Similar complexity to original task - both involve obtaining theme from online source and applying via GNOME settings.
metadata.verification: Verified that gsettings 'org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme' is a valid GNOME setting. Fluent is a well-known GTK theme available on GitHub. Task is feasible and similar to original - both require downloading theme and applying it.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the final state: Fluent theme applied to GNOME desktop
Postconfig uses valid gsettings command to retrieve current GTK theme name
check_list metric appropriately searches for 'Fluent' pattern in gsettings output
Pattern 'Fluent' will match all Fluent variants (Fluent, Fluent-Dark, Fluent-Light, etc.)
Data flow is semantically correct: gsettings output -> cache_file getter -> check_list metric
Evaluator only verifies final state (theme applied), not intermediate steps (download/install from GitHub)
This is a pragmatic verification approach - final state proves task completion regardless of installation source
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor note: Evaluator doesn't distinguish whether theme was downloaded from GitHub vs pre-installed, but this doesn't affect core verification logic since the end result is what matters
